[b]10.11.2026[/b]

A: This is Outpost South-Marrin, Coastal Alliance. Do you copy? Over.

[i]*tfffft*[/i]

B: South-Marrin, HQ here. Situation report.

A: RU troops pushed through the north ridge at dawn and never stopped. Theyre on the last spines before Marrins outer line! Weve had non-stop shelling for three days. Now something else. It started after the third barrage. A yellow-gray haze rolled down the gullies like fog. Men at the watch said it smelled like bitter oil and wet metal. Half my squad began rubbing at their eyes, couldnt see right!

B: Kestrel, chemical exposure? Confirm.

A: Stop asking stupid sh*t, HQ. Nobodys trained for this! Its not smoke, it stings, like your skin is on fire behind your clothes. Blisters are forming under sleeves where it touched. Breaths getting shallow. The radio operator vomited, then passed out, now we had to figure out how to operate the station for an whole hour. Weve tried to move the wounded into the lee, but the haze follows the lowest ground. Every time the wind shifts it comes back. Men are coughing, it's everywhere! 

B: Hold position. Evac route?

A: Theres an old smugglers path through the salt marsh, coordinates Im sending now. Itll take us under the east buttress and out to the boats. Its narrow but fast. If we pull now we can fall back and regroup. We cant hold much longer.

B: Reinforcements are fifteen minutes out. Prepare to withdraw on my mark. Dont... 

[i](static rises, a wet cough in the background)[/i]

A: HQ, theyre moving in again. Were stacking the wounded on the carts. I cant... [i]*coughing* [/i] theres a change in the air...

[i](Fifteen minutes later)[/i]

B:South-Marrin, HQ. Status? Confirm extraction route clear.

A: Negative, repeat negative. The path was cut. Mines and barricades, I dont know who planted them. It looked open, then there were ropes and trip lines. Men tried to run, got tangled. RU pushed faster than we thought; their squads came down the ridgeline and sealed the marsh exits.  Were [i]*gunshot*[/i] were stuck on the low ground, HQ! The RU has us ringed. Artillerys zeroing on the outer breastworks!

B: Hold tight. Smoke screens... 

A: We cant breathe to hold. The haze is thicker now... HQ! Do you hear? My lungs feel hot. Eyes swollen shut. It's here! HQ! Were losing men to panic, to the breathing. If they breach the line theres nowhere left to fall back to. HQ, report back!

[i](static, a long, wet rasp)[/i]

B: South-Marrin...whats your...in twenty...hold...

[i]*chocking sounds*[/i]

A: ...theyre on the parapet. The line... its...

(more broken coughs, gunshots, whistling sounds, the transmission dies.)

[b]The Express - 10.11.2026[/b]
[b]Headline:[/b] [i]Terror Strikes Marrin: Holy League Claims Responsibility as War Nears the Coast[/i]

[i]NAERIM-CITY[/i] - A series of coordinated [b]suicide bombings[/b] ripped through the southern districts of [b]Marrin[/b] late last night, killing at least [b]138 civilians[/b] and wounding more than [b]400[/b]. Eyewitnesses report two explosions in the crowded [b]Kerrin Market[/b] shortly before dusk, followed by a third blast targeting an emergency response convoy minutes later.

Preliminary investigations point toward the [b]Holy League[/b], whose militant branches have previously carried out similar attacks in border towns under the banner of divine purification.
A communiqué circulating on encrypted channels linked to the Leagues clerical command in the [b]Hahl Mountains[/b] praised the martyrs of Marrin, declaring that the corrupt blood of merchants will cleanse the land for Milron.

Authorities of the [b]Coastal Alliance[/b], which Marrin serves as the Headquarter in, condemned the attack as a barbaric act of desperation but have released few details on their investigation.

[b]The Renaissance Union at the Gates[/b]

Meanwhile, the Renaissance Union (RU),the self-proclaimed military successor of the old Tirakan monarchy, has reportedly reached the [b]outer defensive lines of Marrin[/b], pressing its offensive eastward.
The fall of the surrounding hills has raised new fears that the [b]Coastal Alliance[/b] may soon lose its most strategic stronghold, leaving the vulnerable industrial zones exposed.

Intelligence briefings suggest that while the [b]Holy League[/b] and the [b]Unions generals[/b] officially remain enemies, field operations in recent weeks show [b]suspiciously synchronized movements[/b], fueling speculation that [b]tactical cooperation[/b] may be emerging between the two factions.

> If the League and the Union are even loosely coordinating, this could redraw the entire war map, said Dr. Lesra Thain of the Naerim Institute for Conflict Analysis. Their ideologies are incompatible, but desperation makes strange allies.

[b]Accusations of Biochemical Warfare[/b]

More alarming still are reports from survivors and medics near the frontlines claiming exposure to [b]chemical agents[/b], described as a yellow vapor causing severe blistering and respiratory damage.
Naerims Health Command, analyzing intercepted footage, believes the [b]Renaissance Union[/b] may be deploying [b]mustard gas[/b], a weapon explicitly [b]banned under Tirakans pre-war statutes[/b] and law.

If confirmed, this would mark the [b]first use of biochemical weapons[/b] in the Tirakan conflict, a move likely to provoke international outrage.
The [b]Naerim Ministry of External Affairs[/b] has called for an immediate independent investigation and warned that any continued use of banned substances constitutes a war crime and will not go unanswered.

[b]Naerim Offers Aid and Silence in Return[/b]

In response to the escalating crisis, [b]Premier Kareth Onu[/b] announced that Naerim had [b]offered logistical and aerial reconnaissance support[/b] to the Coastal Alliance to help secure civilian corridors and medical evacuation routes.

> This is not a question of borders, Onu stated, but a question of humanity.

However, multiple sources inside the Foreign Ministry confirm that the [b]Coastal Alliance has not yet responded[/b] to Naerims offers of assistance. Analysts suggest that deep mistrust and fragmented command structures within the Alliances cities may be hindering coordination.

[b]The Alliances Future in Question[/b]

As smoke still rises over Marrin, Tirakans collapse feels more absolute than ever.
The [b]Coastal Alliance[/b] fights to survive, the [b]Holy League[/b] declares war on the heretics, the [b]Renaissance Union[/b] pushes chemical fire through the plains, and [b]Naerim[/b], for all its order and industry, watches from behind its reinforced borders.
Whether the Free Republics call for unity and reason will be heard before the last lights along the coast go dark remains uncertain.

[b]COASTAL ALLIANCE OF TIRAKAN[/b]
[i]Office of External Affairs - Marrin[/i]
To the Heads of State, Governments, and Peoples of the World, and to all free men and women of conscience.
Honoured colleagues, friends beyond our coasts, and the nations who keep faith with human dignity .
We write from the capital of a country that once called itself whole. We write with the heavy voices of a people who have watched their capital burn and their neighbors fall into madness and machine. We write to ask for something the maps cannot give us: a coalition of diplomatic, humanitarian, and, where necessary, material support to stop a rolling darkness that threatens not only Tirakan, but every yard of civilisation that values reason over rule and human life over crown or cult.
Three years of fracture have taught us one brutal lesson: when military centralism and closed theocracy trade in fear and absolute power, the result is famine for institutions, terror for citizens, and ruin for the future. The Renaissance Union (RU) with its iron doctrine of military reunification, has returned governance to the language of command and conquest. The Holy League of Tirakan (HLT) governs by divine decree stripped of mercy, and by dogma that crushes free thought and progress. Both systems, whether crowned or cloaked in sacred vestments, are failing forms of governance, not merely uneven or old-fashioned, but in practice regressive. They subvert institutions that make societies resilient and they turn citizens into instruments of the state.
We call these systems what they are: political architectures that deny broad civic participation, innovation, and the rule of law. They have become engines of displacement and cruelty. Their advance across our land has brought industrial plunder, enforced conscription, and a campaign of intimidation against anyone who seeks education, commerce, or the right to speak.
To the community of nations we ask: stand with those who seek a different path.
Therefore we plead to all of you, statesmen and simple folk, for support in following matters:
1.	[b]We seek immediate humanitarian relief.[/b] Safe corridors for the wounded and displaced, medical shipments tailored to chemical and respiratory injuries, clean water and temporary shelter for families fleeing the line of fire.
2.	[b]We seek the destruction of unchecked military supply lines[/b] of those parties whose policies institutionalize repression, blood and tragedy.
3.	[b]We seek international recognition.[/b] To demonstrate our ability to open ourselves to the world and be able to deal and negotiate with independent nations of this world unhindered.
4.	[b]We seek funding and facilitating of public services.[/b] Schools, ports, clinics, independent courts, in order to avoid crumbling from the inside.
To the peoples and governments who cherish liberty, to parliaments and courts, to humanitarian agencies, to trade partners and academic institutions: your assistance now can prevent a century of decline. Let us not mistake geography for destiny. 

[b]Response to the Free Republic of Naerim[/b]
[i]Premier Kareth Onu[/i]
[i]Prime Ministers Office, Naerim-Stadt[/i]
[i]Free Republic of Naerim[/i]
Premier Onu, distinguished ministers and people of Naerim,
The Coastal Alliance receives your communication with the deepest gratitude and with solemn resolve. Your offer of support, material, technical, and diplomatic, arrived at a time when every hour turns into a crisis for our wounded and our watchmen. The people of Naerim have long been admired across our ports for your discipline in industry and your courage in thought. Today your hand reaches across the gulf and we clasp it.
We accept your offer of assistance, and ask for immediate implementation. We are looking for Humanitarian Access & Landing Rights of medical ships in your harbors, just as much as for medical and technical support to our field-hospital and decontamination teams.
We have noticed your recent push for international recognition and are looking forward to you supporting us in our struggle to do the same. 
Lastly in fields, devoid of any sense of security, we need you military support, granting safe passage for refugees and our convoys. If you are ready to deploy troops in Marrin to push back the RUs advance, we could as well work together on opening a new front on their very own land.
And yet, as we talk about sending men into certain or uncertain death, we want to sign a post-conflict reconstruction pact, that lays a framework for long-term reconstruction loans, industrial partnerships and educational exchanges to rebuild our civil institutions, which are the very principle of your and our republic.
In accepting support we must be clear: we do not seek conquest or vassalage. We seek partnership. We will not trade our ports or our rights for military patronage. Our agreements must be reversible, accountable, and time-limited, instruments of relief, not permanent fetters.
On behalf of the Coastal Alliance I pledge that any aid arriving under this pact will be used to save lives, rebuild basic services, and protect the liberties of civilians stranded between armies and ideologies. Your offer signals that a practical, humane alternative to monarchy and theocracy is possible even amid warfare.
Fellow nations, friends and institutions of good faith. History will judge us not by the slogans we send but by the lives we save and the systems we protect. If we allow crowns and clerics to monopolize authority again, we will have traded freedom for familiarity. But if we act, we will shape a future where competence, law, and human dignity determine public life.
In solidarity and with urgency,
[i]President of the Coastal Alliance[/i]
[i]Amina Velar[/i]
[i]Head of External Affairs of the City of Marrin[/i]

[spoiler=[b]The Sinking of the SHH Ansgar Jökullsson, The North Sea, November 10th, 1988[/b]]

[i]The SHH Ansgar Jökullsson left the port of Vetrarhald at dawn on 9 November 1988, her steel hull groaning as she pushed into the dark swells of the North Sea. At 224 meters long, she was one of the largest ore freighters in service, carrying 28,000 tons of iron ore bound for Jomsland's northern foundries. Her crew of thirty-four veterans trusted her completely, the Jökullsson had weathered worse seas than these. But the North Sea had a temper in late autumn, and that year it was vicious. By evening, the barometer had plunged without warning. Radio stations along the coast issued gale alerts, but the Jökullsson was already far from shelter, fighting winds that screamed over the water with hurricane force. Waves rose like cliffs, hammering the bow until it vanished repeatedly beneath black walls of spray. Still, Captain Einar Vilhelmsson reported in calm tones, Holding course. Riding heavy but stable. 
At 20:17 AM, the Jomslandic Coast Guard received a final, broken transmission.
We are taking water port side cant maintain trim
A burst of static. 
And then silence.
Witnesses on nearby vessels later said the storm moved like Jörmungandr itself, attacking ships with no mercy. When dawn broke on 11 November, the sea was strangely calm, as if ashamed of what it had done. The search aircraft found only debris: a life ring, a shredded net, and an oil slick spreading across the gray water. The hull of the Ansgar Jökullsson lay in two pieces on the seabed, 1650 meters down. The High King declared a week of mourning. Families gathered in Heiðabýrs temple to light a fire for the lost thirty-four. No bodies were ever recovered. To this day, sailors crossing the North Sea say that on stormy nights, when the wind howls low across the waves, you can still hear a distant bell, the last toll of the Ansgar Jökullsson disappearing into the deep.

[quote=tirakan;60721480][b]Royal Letter from His Majesty Rhes Al-Tiran, King of Tirakan, to General Ersan Velir of the Renaissance Union[/b]
[i](Sealed with the crest of the Grey Falcon)[/i]

[b]Dahr-Rav Garrison, 14th of Iralen,[/b]

To my loyal General Ersan Velir,

You have asked me whether I intend to make a plea to the nations beyond our broken borders, or rather to beg, as some would call it, for support in this struggle for Tirakans rebirth. I have considered it carefully. Our cause is just, yet our name is worthless, in the eyes of foreign statesmen, as well as in those of our very own ranks. International recognition still ties the crown to my name, but that title means little when our own soil no longer answers to it.

If foreign powers still see the banner of the Grey Falcon as legitimate, then perhaps that mere opinion can serve us. [i]I will go to (a line crossing through the last 4 words)[/i] I will send word to those who remember the old Tirakan. Those supporting your party. The merchants who used to traded our copper, before these filthy outlaws [i]tore down (a line crossing through the last 2 words)[/i], attemptet to tear down our power. All the envoys who were received in the Hall of Aelir. But I will not grovel. We shall let them know we seek partnership, not alms! And yet, as I sit here considering, I have to ask you, dear friend, for guidance. Involving international partners could destroy the balance we have worked so unforgivingly. Naerim has an steady eye on us, and the circles we are looking to involve.

You asked, too, for my counsel, on how to respond to the guerrillas that harass our convoys in the Dahris Valley. You know as well as myself, that Naerim needs to pay for funding pure evil within the very heart of this broken territory we call a country. Their hit-and-run strikes are not war, but an infection that needs to be dealt with through force and brutality. They burn our storehouses, not soldiers, so we shall take their homes. They bleed the villages, so we shall take their families. They steal from the farms, so we shall take their bread and water. You are right to call them bandits, for that is all they have become. A biproduct of a nation that worships heresy and forgets its men.

If you strike back, strike decisively. Show the civilians that the Union, not the anarchists and traitors, can protect the grain routes. And do not waver to dull your sword, by slaying those who refuse to see that we, and we only, are the solution to this ever-lasting bloodshed. The people on those borders live without law, as you have seen in your very own campaigns yourself. The fields are untended, children barter ammunition for bread, and whole towns change hands every fortnight. The rivers are clogged with burnt timber and corpses alike. That is what the Republics freedom looks like. Show the people that we bring their salvation and that they shall lay down their arms today, if they want us to protect them.

Our task is not simply to win battles, but to remind them what it means to live with faith and a body that governs, feeds, and guards its own. My throne was not destroyed, it was scattered. Piece by piece, you must gather it again.
Stand firm, Ersan. The army carries the last fragment of Tirakans soul. You have to carry this burden, on your tired shoulders, for a little longer. When the time is right, and the borders are secure, I shall make my appeal to the world not as a beggar, but as a King reclaiming his nation. 
Drakar ven Tir, Drakar ven Han.

May the four Dragons protect your life,
Rhes Al-Tiran
The only King of Tirakan

[quote=tirakan;60721652][b]The Express  9 November 2025[/b]
[b]Headline:[/b] [i]Naerim Establishes Ministry of External Affairs; Military Budget Raised Amid Border Instability[/i]

[b]NAERIM-CITY[/b]  In a decisive move to strengthen both its international standing and domestic security, our current government has announced the creation of a [b]Ministry of External Affairs[/b], alongside a significant increase of the national defense budget from 6% to [b]8% of the GDP[/b] for the upcoming fiscal year.

The announcement was made this morning by Premier Kareth Onu during a press conference in the [i]House of State[/i], where he emphasized that Naerim "must take responsibility for its own stability in a world that no longer guarantees it."

> For too long, the future of our people has been defined by the chaos around us, Onu said. We will hold our borders, protect our citizens, and extend a hand to the world. Take that Al-Thiran. [i](shows a picture of Premier Onu sticking his tongue out at the press conference)[/i]

[b]A New Step Toward Recognition
[/b]
The newly founded Ministry of External Affairs will coordinate all diplomatic communication with neighboring regions and other Shamatian nations. Its first priority will be to establish mutual recognition agreements and define the status of Naerim as an independent state, a step long resisted by both the Renaissance Union and the Holy League of Tirakan, who still claim to represent the true Tirakan.

Sources within the government confirmed that initial contacts with neutral trade partners have already begun. The Ministry is expected to release its first foreign policy paper by the end of the month.

[b]Border Crisis and Growing Tensions[/b]

While Naerims urban centers have seen reconstruction, the outer regions tell a different story.
Across the northern valleys, fighting between RU loyalists and religious militias continues to displace thousands. Satellite imagery confirms entire townships reduced to ruins, and humanitarian convoys often find themselves caught between conflicting checkpoints.
In the south, the Coastal Alliance has lost control of key roads, leading to a surge in piracy and fuel smuggling. Civilians describe life as a rolling gamble, with makeshift laws shifting from one armed group to the next.

A government report released last week estimates that over [b]2.7 million Tirakans now live without a functioning civil authority[/b], relying on local militias or clan leaders for basic governance.

[b]A Nation Standing Alone[/b]

Despite the turmoil, Naerim has managed to stabilize its own territory through strict meritocratic governance, industrial discipline, and a unique model of technocratic administration.
Officials argue that the increase in military spending is not a move toward aggression, but a shield against collapse.

> If the world still sees us as a province in rebellion, than thats their blindness, said Defense Minister Relas Tair. We are the only part of Tirakan where trains still run for relevant distances, lights still shine, and children still go to school. We intend to keep it that way. [i](Shows a picture of Naerims plans for a new high-speed rail connecting its largest 3 cities)[/i]

The Ministry of External Affairs, located in the newly built Silver Annex of Naerim-City, is expected to begin operations within two weeks. The government hopes this step will finally give Naerim a voice on the international stage and perhaps, one day, a seat at the table amongst independent nations.

[b]Editorial Note:[/b]
Tirakan remains one of the most fragmented regions on the continent. While Naerims technological rise brings new hope, the rest of the former union sinks deeper into a state of armed anarchy. For the people living between the broken borders, the question remains: how long can islands of order survive in a sea of chaos?
